newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Cimpor seeks foreign cement firms-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Cimpor seeks foreign cement firms-analysts.

text.p: Portugal's biggest cement producer Cimpor is hunting for further foreign acquisitions after snatching five percent of the growing Brazilian market with deals worth $400 million, analysts said on Tuesday.
In its first foray into Brazil, cash-rich Cimpor acquired CISAFRA, a cement producer, and the SERRANA group's cement business, for 62 billion escudos ($384 million) last week.
Analysts believe Cimpor won't stop there and may seek further cement firms in Brazil, a huge and fragmented market, other South American countries, southern Africa and Spain.

"Cimpor's strategy is to diversify geographically and take advantage of different economic cycles in each market," said Manuel Puerta da Costa, analyst with Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI) in Oporto.
Cimpor has the potential to invest up to 250 billion escudos in foreign acquisitions up to 2001, a company source said recently, before the Brazilian deals were announced.

Diario de Noticias newspaper reported on Monday that Cimpor was interested in acquiring a Spanish cement manufacturer, perhaps close to the border with Portugal so that it could serve both markets easily. Cimpor officials declined comment.
Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal already owns Spanish cement firm Corporacion Noroeste, which operates in northwestern Spain.
Last August Cimpor bought Moroccan cement firm Asment Temara for 11.8 billion escudos. It also owns a subsidiary in Mozambique, Empresa de Cimentos de Mocambique.
Puerta da Costa said he expected Cimpor to achieve between 42 and 45 percent of its sales abroad in 2000, up from 38 percent this year following the Brazilian acquisitions.
James Harrison of Lisbon broker Midas said Cimpor's debt to total assets ratio stood at 16 percent after the Brazilian acquisitions, below its self-imposed limit of 30 percent.

He said this gave Cimpor leeway to make further acquisitions worth up to $200 million this year if it found the right company. "If Cimpor find the right company, they'll buy it. If they don't, they won't," he said.

Analysts said Cimpor bought the Brazilian businesses for a good price, $176.7 per ton of production capacity, and this helped lift the stock to an all-time high of 3,925 escudos on Lisbon bourse when the deal was announced on January 15.
Demand for cement in Brazil was expected to grow by up to seven percent per year until 2000, analysts said.
Cimpor said that the production capacity of the Brazilian businesses would reach about three million tons per year.
The two businesses were presently operating at about 60 percent capacity, analysts said.
"Cimpor wants to increase capacity utilisation in its Brazilian businesses," Harrison said. "With the level of growth expected in Brazil, they will have paid a good price."
Puerta da Costa said: "This will turn out to be a good price in the medium term."

Cimpor said its cement production capacity in Portugal, Spain, Mozambique, Morocco and Brazil would stand at 11 million tons per year and total sales would be nine million tons per year after the Brazilian acquisitions.
Analysts said they expected the Cimpor share price to outperform the Lisbon exchange and hit 4,500 escudos by the end of 1997.
Cimpor shares stood at 3,785 escudos, down 80, in volume of 153,056 shares in afternoon trade on Tuesday.
